hook.en: Using the patient's own gentle muscle contractions, with your hand resistance, to improve range, strength and control.
hook.ur: PNF manual techniques mein therapist ki resistance, stretch aur diagonal movement patterns use hotay hain taake coordinated movement aur functional motor control ko facilitate kiya ja sake.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what PNF Manual Techniques is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke PNF Manual Techniques kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation (PNF) uses diagonal movement patterns and carefully timed muscle contractions against your resistance. Techniques include hold-relax, contract-relax, rhythmic initiation, slow reversal and rhythmic stabilization. They are used to gain range, teach control and build strength.
text.ur: Manual resistance, stretch aur diagonal movement patterns ke zariye coordinated movement aur functional motor control ko facilitate kiya jata hai.

simpler.en: Using the patient's own gentle muscle contractions, with your hand resistance, to improve range, strength and control.
simpler.ur: PNF manual techniques mein therapist ki resistance, stretch aur diagonal movement patterns use hotay hain taake coordinated movement aur functional motor control ko facilitate kiya ja sake.

text.en: Like a coach guiding a swing: you provide just enough resistance and timing for the muscles to coordinate, and then the athlete does the work.
text.ur: Jaise coach swing (bat ya golf) guide karta hai: aap bas utni resistance aur timing dete hain jitni muscles ko coordinate hone ke liye chahiye, phir asal kaam athlete khud karta hai.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Muscles work in diagonal, spiral patterns (D1 and D2) that match daily and sports movement.
**2.** After a gentle contraction, a muscle may stretch more easily, so you gain range right after it.
**3.** Verbal commands, touch and resistance combine to guide the movement.
text.ur: Task-specific sensory input, resistance aur patterned movement motor output ko influence kar sakte hain. Techniques mein rhythmic initiation, repeated contractions, hold-relax, contract-relax, stabilizing reversals aur rhythmic stabilization shamil hain. PNF ek flexible clinical framework hai, sirf ek technique nahi.

question.en: Vocabulary first — clinicians use this word a lot. What does **D1 / D2 patterns** mean?
question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **D1 / D2 patterns** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en: Diagonal movement patterns of the arm or leg that combine flexion or extension with rotation.
text.ur: Diagonal movement patterns of the arm or leg that combine flexion or extension with rotation.

text.en:
So when does **PNF Manual Techniques** make sense?
• Muscle tightness limiting range (hamstrings, calves, shoulder muscles).
• Weakness or poor control after injury or surgery.
• Neurological rehabilitation, where guided movement patterns help motor learning.
text.ur: Neurological rehabilitation, sports aur orthopedic rehabilitation, aur movement coordination deficits.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Uncontrolled high blood pressure or heart conditions (avoid strong breath-holding).
• Acute muscle tear, unstable fracture or joint instability.
• Pain that increases during the contraction.
text.ur:
Painful acute injury aur sustained isometrics ke sath cardiovascular limitations.
Jab medical ya surgical restrictions ki wajah se movement ya contraction mana ho.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Explain and demonstrate
steps.detail: Show the movement pattern and what you want them to do.

steps.title: Move to the first restriction
steps.detail: Example: lift the straight leg to the point where the hamstring feels tight.

steps.title: Ask for a gentle contraction
steps.detail: 'Push gently into my hand.' Use a light to moderate effort and breathe normally.

steps.title: Hold, then relax
steps.detail: Hold about 5-10 seconds, then tell them to fully relax.

steps.title: Move to the new range
steps.detail: Take the leg further into the freshly available range and hold briefly.

steps.title: Repeat and retest
steps.detail: Repeat 3-5 times and retest range or function.

beats.ur:
1. Functional goal aur relevant diagonal ya movement pattern select karein.
2. Therapist ke contacts aise rakhein ke direction guide ho aur dard na ho.
3. Verbal cues, visual tracking aur graded manual resistance use karein.
4. Mobility, movement initiation, strength ya stability ke goal ke mutabiq PNF technique choose karein.
5. Behtari ko kisi functional task mein apply karwayein.

question.en: Imagine the patient is in front of you. What do you do FIRST?
question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

feedback.en: Right — this comes first. Show the movement pattern and what you want them to do.
feedback.ur: Sahi — sab se pehle yehi. Show the movement pattern and what you want them to do.

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: a gentle contraction of about 5-10 seconds followed by a 10-30 second stretch, repeated 3-5 times. Keep effort light to moderate.
text.ur: Aam tor par achi quality wali repetitions ke chhote sets aur darmiyan mein rest. Resistance itni ho ke movement smooth rahe; jab tak specifically strength test na ho, maximum effort ki zaroorat nahi.

beats.patient: Jamal, 24, footballer, tight left hamstring; straight leg raise stops at 60 degrees.
beats.assessment: Pain-free, tight sensation behind the thigh, no tear signs.
beats.treatment: Contract-relax: at 60 degrees he pushes his heel gently into your shoulder for 8 seconds, relaxes, you lift the leg further. Repeat 4 times.
beats.reassess: Raise improves to 75 degrees. He follows with active hamstring control exercises.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein patient ko chair se uthte waqt movement coordinate karne mein mushkil hoti hai. Therapist suitable pattern aur graded resistance practice karwa kar chair se uthne ka task dobara assess karta hai. Yeh sirf learning example hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Asking for a maximum contraction.
• Letting the patient hold their breath.
• Stretching straight away without full relaxation.
text.ur: Pattern ko patient ke goal se alag practice karna, fatigue ignore karna aur pain ke through movement force karna avoid karein. Task ko patient ki ability ke mutabiq simplify karein aur quality, symptoms aur effort monitor karein.

text.en: PNF stretching can improve flexibility in the short term, similar to other stretching methods. Mechanisms likely include changes in stretch tolerance rather than only muscle lengthening.
text.ur: Progress ko relevant functional task, coordination, strength ya activity tolerance se measure karein. PNF ko guaranteed neurological recovery technique na kahein; diagnosis-specific evidence aur broader rehab plan ko saath rakhein.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Gentle contraction, full relaxation, then move into the new range.**
text.ur: Pattern function ko behtar banane ke liye use karein; diagonal movement khud final goal nahi.
